Economic stability

Some basic purposes of spending in the way of Allah are: (a) purification of the self; (b) a means of guidance; (c) social welfare and wellbeing; (d) economic stability.

Islam has emphasised to Muslims the earning of livelihood. For example, in Surah al-Jumu‘ah He said that when you are free from the performance of prayer, then spread out in the earth and seek the bounty of Allah. In the same way in Surah al-‘Ankabut it was said that those idols which you worship besides Allah are not the owners of your sustenance; therefore you should seek sustenance only from your Lord. The saying of the Noble Prophet ﷺ too is:

مَا اَكَلَ اَحَدٌ مِّنْ بَنِيْ آدَمَ طَعَامًا خَيْرًا لَّهٗ مِنْ اَنْ يَّاْكُلَ مِنْ عَمَلِ يَدِهٖ وَاِنَّ نَبِيَّ اللّٰهِ دَاوٗدَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ كَانَ يَاْكُلُ مِنْ كَسْبِ يَدِهٖ (صحیح بخاری: 2072)

Translation: Among the children of Adam, the food of that person is most full of good and blessing who eats his livelihood from the earning of his own hands; and the Prophet of Allah Most High, Dawud (peace be upon him), too used to eat from the earning of his own hands.

Islam has not only given encouragement for earning a livelihood but has also settled basic rules for earning a livelihood, some important ones of which are as follows:

1. Earning livelihood by a permissible and recognised method.

2. Keeping away from interest-based business.

3. Avoiding deceit, adulteration and impermissible profiteering.

4. Refraining from the lust for wealth.

5. Not taking possession of someone’s property by a false method.

6. Abandoning evils like bribery.

7. Paying zakat, charity and alms out of the wealth earned.

Economic stability

Some basic purposes of spending in the way of Allah are: (a) purification of the self; (b) a means of guidance; (c) social welfare and wellbeing; (d) economic stability.

Islam has emphasised to Muslims the earning of livelihood. For example, in Surah al-Jumu‘ah He said that when you are free from the performance of prayer, then spread out in the earth and seek the bounty of Allah. In the same way in Surah al-‘Ankabut it was said that those idols which you worship besides Allah are not the owners of your sustenance; therefore you should seek sustenance only from your Lord. The saying of the Noble Prophet ﷺ too is:

مَا اَكَلَ اَحَدٌ مِّنْ بَنِيْ آدَمَ طَعَامًا خَيْرًا لَّهٗ مِنْ اَنْ يَّاْكُلَ مِنْ عَمَلِ يَدِهٖ وَاِنَّ نَبِيَّ اللّٰهِ دَاوٗدَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ كَانَ يَاْكُلُ مِنْ كَسْبِ يَدِهٖ (صحیح بخاری: 2072)

Translation: Among the children of Adam, the food of that person is most full of good and blessing who eats his livelihood from the earning of his own hands; and the Prophet of Allah Most High, Dawud (peace be upon him), too used to eat from the earning of his own hands.

Islam has not only given encouragement for earning a livelihood but has also settled basic rules for earning a livelihood, some important ones of which are as follows:

1. Earning livelihood by a permissible and recognised method.

2. Keeping away from interest-based business.

3. Avoiding deceit, adulteration and impermissible profiteering.

4. Refraining from the lust for wealth.

5. Not taking possession of someone’s property by a false method.

6. Abandoning evils like bribery.

7. Paying zakat, charity and alms out of the wealth earned.

8. Avoiding israf, i.e. not adopting extravagance (tabdhir).

9. Eating good and pure things and avoiding impure things.

10. Above all, considering Allah Most High alone the real Sustainer and knowing one’s efforts and wisdom to be His gift.

11. Distributing out of the property granted by Him, in His way, among deprived classes.

From the above-mentioned points it is proved that the economic system of Islam provides the guarantee of economic stability. By paying zakat and charities the lust and greed for property and wealth ends from the heart of man. In this way his purification of the self takes place. The saying of the Exalted is:

خُذْ مِنْ اَمْوَالِهِمْ صَدَقَةً تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيْهِمْ بِهَا (التوبہ: 103)

Translation: O Prophet, take charity from their property and purify them and purify their selves.

When the self of wealthy people is purified, then they do not take part in such economic activities as become the cause of economic instability or from which harm reaches the interest of the common people.

In brief we can say that by spending in the way of Allah the economic system gets stability. Economic unevenness becomes less and the problems of deprived classes become somewhat less, from which they become a cause of increase in national productive capacities.

Responsibilities of the individual and society

With reference to spending in the way of Allah some responsibilities fall on the individual and society, without fulfilling which social and economic stability cannot be established.

1. The first responsibility that falls on every individual is that he spend all his energies for earning a livelihood. He should leave no stone unturned in bringing his abilities into use.

2. The second responsibility is that for earning wealth he should keep in view the basic teachings of Islam. Islam has certainly given encouragement for earning a livelihood, but it has also settled basic rules in business life. The wealth earned by means of interest, or the profit obtained by adulteration, or property obtained from prohibited sources in the same way — Islam has declared it forbidden. Property earned in this way, even if all of it is spent in the way of Allah, there is no benefit of it in the hereafter.

۲۔ دوسری ذمہ داری یہ ہے کہ دولت کمانے کے لیے اسلام کی بنیادی تعلیمات کو مدِنظر رکھے۔ اسلام نے کسبِ معاش کی ترغیب ضرور دی ہے لیکن کاروبارِ زندگی میں بنیادی ضابطے بھی طے کر دیے ہیں۔ سود کے ذریعے کمائی ہوئی دولت، یا ملاوٹ سے حاصل کیا گیا منافع یا اسی طرح ممنوع ذرائع سے حاصل شدہ مال، اسلام نے حرام قرار دیا ہے۔ اس طرح کمایا گیا مال بے شک سارے کا سارا راہِ اللہ میں خرچ کر دیا جائے اس کا کوئی اُخروی فائدہ نہیں ہے۔
